body.statement: If \(\tau_n\to\infty\) and \(b_n\to b\in\mathbb R\), then \(\{L^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}\widehat\Delta^P_{\ell}-\overline\Delta\}/\sqrt{\rho_n\overline V/n}\Rightarrow N(b,1)\), while replacing \(\widehat\Delta^P_{\ell}\) by \(\widehat\Delta^E_{\ell}\) gives \(N(0,1)\). Aggregate first-order equivalence holds if and only if \(b_n\to0\), even when individual pairwise shifts do not vanish.
body.justification: The exact signed aggregate criterion preserves cross-pair cancellation that a maximum pairwise bound would erase.
body.gap: The published fifteen-pair aggregation assumes interior regularity and has no rare-link noncentrality frontier.
body.consumer: The fixed fifteen-comparison crime aggregate can be assessed without requiring every individual comparison to be safely away from link disagreement.
body.proof_tex:
Let
\[
\overline{\widehat\Delta}^{,P}=L^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^L\widehat\Delta^P_\ell,
\qquad
\overline{\widehat\Delta}^{,E}=L^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^L\widehat\Delta^E_\ell,
\qquad
\overline\Delta^{,P}=L^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^L\Delta^P_\ell.
\]
The centered Taylor and characteristic-function argument in the pairwise proof does not require convergence of the drifting cancellation indices.  It gives, jointly over the fixed pairs,
\[
\frac{\widehat\Delta^P_\ell-\Delta^P_\ell}{\sqrt{\rho_n/n}}
\Rightarrow N(0,V_\ell),
\qquad
\frac{\widehat\Delta^E_\ell-\Delta_\ell}{\sqrt{\rho_n/n}}
\Rightarrow N(0,V_\ell),
\]
with independent coordinates.  Since
\(
\overline V=L^{-2}\sum_{\ell=1}^LV_\ell>0,
\)
finite-dimensional characteristic functions therefore give
\[
\frac{\overline{\widehat\Delta}^{,P}-\overline\Delta^{,P}}
{\sqrt{\rho_n\overline V/n}}\Rightarrow N(0,1),
\qquad
\frac{\overline{\widehat\Delta}^{,E}-\overline\Delta}
{\sqrt{\rho_n\overline V/n}}\Rightarrow N(0,1).
\tag{1}
\]
By the definition of \(b_n\), the exact deterministic centering difference is
\[
\frac{\overline\Delta^{,P}-\overline\Delta}
{\sqrt{\rho_n\overline V/n}}
=\frac{\sqrt{n/\rho_n}}{L\sqrt{\overline V}}
\sum_{\ell=1}^L(\Delta^P_\ell-\Delta_\ell)=b_n.
\tag{2}
\]
Adding (2) to the first convergence in (1) proves the \(N(b,1)\) limit whenever \(b_n\to b\).  The second convergence in (1) proves the centered exact-link limit.

The gradient comparison in the pairwise proof is uniform over the finite set of pairs, so summing its Taylor expansions yields
\[
\frac{\overline{\widehat\Delta}^{,P}-\overline{\widehat\Delta}^{,E}}
{\sqrt{\rho_n\overline V/n}}=b_n+o_P(1).
\tag{3}
\]
Thus aggregate first-order equivalence is equivalent to \(b_n\to0\), not to coordinatewise vanishing of all pairwise shifts.

For completeness, the distinction is nonvacuous.  Take two pairs with \((c_1,c_2,c_3)=(2,2,1)\) and \((1/2,4,1)\), respectively, and put all remaining pairs on a cancellation plane.  The two nonzero leading signed coefficients satisfy
\[
Q_1A_1=4(\log2)^2,
\qquad Q_2A_2=-4(\log2)^2.
\]
Along a sequence with \(\sqrt{\tau_n}=u_n^3\), the uniform expansion makes their summed population shift \(O(\rho_nu_n^{-4})\), and hence \(b_n=O(u_n^{-1})\to0\), whereas each individual standardized leading shift has magnitude of order \(u_n\).  Integer \(n\) may be chosen along a subsequence with \(n\rho_n/u_n^6\to1\).  This exhibits aggregate cancellation while neither individual shift vanishes.
